decisions.decision: Town to approach the 101 Pleasant Street owner and/or his engineer about remediating 225 Pleasant Street at their expense; if they refuse, the Town will take legal action for damages. Ms. Lafleur and Mr. Burney assigned to address it.
decisions.quote: ms. lafleur and mr. burney will address this task.

decisions.decision: The Board signed the five Annual Town Meeting warrants for posting.
decisions.quote: the board signed the five warrants for the annual town meeting posting.

decisions.decision: The Board signed an accounts payable warrant.
decisions.quote: the board signed an accounts payable warrant in the amount of $373,303.60.

decisions.decision: Suggested amendment to the Town Manager evaluation form was not agreed on; the form will not be changed midway through the process.
decisions.quote: suggestion made to amend the form tonight was not agreed on because it would not be fair to the town manager to change the form midway through the process.

decisions.decision: The Board agreed to hold workshops once a month, with workshop topics scheduled in advance.
decisions.quote: the board agreed. the workshops and topics should be scheduled in advance so research can be done in preparation.

budget_items.topic: DPW sale of rain barrels and compost bins
budget_items.what_was_recorded: Ms. Luck reported prices for rain barrels and compost bins sold at the DPW, payable by cash or check.
budget_items.quote: compost bins are $43 and rain barrels are $56.

budget_items.what_was_recorded: Ms. Luck corrected a newspaper report about her vote on placing the $4 million debt exclusion article for pavement management on the ballot.
budget_items.quote: reported that she had voted against placing the $4 million debt exclusion article for pavement management on the ballot.

budget_items.topic: Curbside yard waste pickup cost to residents
budget_items.what_was_recorded: Ms. Luck asked whether residents would be willing to pay extra for bi-weekly curbside yard waste pickup; no figure was given.
budget_items.quote: ms. luck asked ms. lehtinen if she and others would be willing to pay extra for this service.

budget_items.what_was_recorded: Rep. Benson reported the Governor's budget has a 3.5% increase and the House budget will have a 3% increase.
budget_items.quote: the governor's budget has a 3.5% percent increase and the house budget will have a 3% increase.

budget_items.what_was_recorded: Rep. Benson reported local aid has a 4.6% increase in the Governor's budget and education aid a 1.6% increase; the delegation will file an amendment to fully fund Chapter 40S.
budget_items.quote: local aid has a 4.6% increase in the governor's budget. education aid was only a 1.6% increase

budget_items.what_was_recorded: Discussion of the Chapter 70 increase, phase-in of foundation formula changes, and the millionaires' tax as a possible revenue source not available until 2017; Mr. Alonzo asked for a partial deferral.
budget_items.quote: the 11.5% increase in chapter 70 does not take into account the increase that you would see here in town.

budget_items.what_was_recorded: Mr. Alonzo reported three contingency items approved (maintenance garage, air cooling system, digital sign for Mass Ave.) at a total cost of approximately $740,000.
budget_items.quote: total cost of these 3 items is approximately $740,000.

budget_items.what_was_recorded: The Board signed an accounts payable warrant in the stated amount.
budget_items.quote: the board signed an accounts payable warrant in the amount of $373,303.60.
